claim: FDA grants full approval to Leqembi (lecanemab) for Alzheimer's disease treatment
approach_a:
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has granted traditional (full) approval to Leqembi (lecanemab-irmb) for the treatment of Alzheimer’s disease, marking a significant milestone in the fight against this progressive neurological condition. Originally approved under the accelerated pathway, Leqembi has now achieved full approval based on confirmatory clinical trial data demonstrating its ability to slow cognitive decline in patients with early Alzheimer’s disease. As the first amyloid beta-directed antibody to make this transition from accelerated to traditional approval, Leqembi is indicated for adults with mild cognitive impairment or mild dementia due to Alzheimer’s who have confirmed presence of elevated brain amyloid, a hallmark of the disease.

Leqembi works by targeting and clearing amyloid plaques in the brain, a core pathological feature of Alzheimer’s. The full FDA approval not only validates its clinical benefit but also supports broader access, as Medicare has indicated it will cover the treatment for appropriate patients. Additionally, the FDA has approved a new subcutaneous injection version, Leqembi IQLIK®, offering a more convenient at-home dosing option for both initiation and maintenance therapy. This advancement represents a pivotal development in Alzheimer’s care, providing a scientifically proven treatment that modifies the disease’s course and improves outcomes for patients in its early stages.

sub_claims: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has issued a full approval (as opposed to accelerated or emergency use) for the drug Leqembi (lecanemab) for the treatment of Alzheimer's disease.
Leqembi (lecanemab) is approved for use in patients diagnosed with mild cognitive impairment or mild dementia due to Alzheimer's disease.
The FDA's full approval of Leqembi was based on clinical trial data demonstrating a statistically significant reduction in cognitive decline compared to placebo over an 18-month period.

The approval includes specific dosing guidelines, administration method (intravenous infusion), and recommended monitoring for treatment-related side effects such as amyloid-related imaging abnormalities (ARIA).
Leqembi (lecanemab) is the first disease-modifying therapy for Alzheimer's disease to receive full FDA approval.
